title: Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce
subtitle: golden, sweet-savoury chicken skewers with a creamy coconut peanut sauce, rice and cool cucumber
imageAlt: Golden chicken satay skewers with a bowl of peanut sauce, white rice and sliced cucumber on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Soak wooden skewers in water 30 minutes so they don't burn, or use metal ones.
Thaw frozen chicken thighs in the fridge overnight.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, turmeric, cumin and oil. Cover and chill 20 minutes or up to a day.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Skewer and bake
steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with a rack in the upper third. Thread the chicken onto 12 skewers and lay them on a foil-lined baking sheet. Bake 12–14 minutes, turning once, until browned at the edges and 74°C (165°F).

steps.title: Peanut sauce
steps.text: Whisk the peanut butter, coconut milk, soy sauce, brown sugar, 1 tbsp lime juice and garlic powder in a small pot over medium-low 2–3 minutes until smooth and warm. Thin with water if needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the skewers over rice with the cucumber slices and a bowl of peanut sauce for dipping.

fixIt.fix: Whisk in warm water 1 tbsp at a time.
Soak wooden skewers longer, or cover the bare ends with foil.
Broil 2 minutes at the end, watching closely.

saleTip: Boneless thighs are cheapest in No Frills value packs; peanut butter is often $4.99 for 1 kg.
swap: Chicken breasts: bake 10–12 minutes to 74°C (165°F). Air fryer: 200°C for 10–12 minutes, turning once.
leftovers: Slide the chicken off the skewers for rice bowls or wraps with the sauce.
doneness: Chicken thighs at 74°C (165°F) (Health Canada, poultry pieces).
source: Based on tested oven chicken satay methods (RecipeTin Eats, Canadian Living): turmeric-and-soy marinated thigh strips on skewers, baked hot; a coconut peanut sauce. Kept mild with no chili.
prepAhead: Marinate the chicken up to 1 day ahead.
Make the peanut sauce up to 5 days ahead; it thickens in the fridge, so thin it when warming.
reheat: Chicken covered in the microwave 1–2 minutes, until 74°C (165°F); warm the sauce separately.

basic.note: Soy-garlic chicken skewers with peanut sauce and rice; no turmeric, cumin or cucumber.

stepNotes.0: Basic: skip the turmeric and cumin.

fancy.note: Quick-pickled cucumber and chopped peanuts over the sauce.

stepNotes.1: Fancy: toss the cucumber with the rice vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt; let it sit while the rice cooks.

addSteps.title: Peanuts
addSteps.text: Scatter the chopped peanuts over the peanut sauce.

plating: Peanut sauce in a small bowl.

why.0-4: Turmeric gives satay its golden colour; it's earthy, not hot.
why.0-0: Thighs stay juicy in a very hot oven.
why.1-1: Coconut milk makes the peanut sauce silky and pourable.

funFact: Satay is street food across Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore, traditionally grilled over charcoal.

keeps.note: freeze the cooked chicken; sauce keeps 5 days in the fridge
